engagement_title: NORTHGROVE fall capsule launch: two mornings of flat-lays and a photographed club pennant into a buyer lookbook, a poster pair, a shoppable set and a hang-tag run
vertical: Fashion and apparel, heritage workwear capsule with cast metal hardware, wholesale to independent stockists plus direct sale (Burlington, Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: Four real postings are absorbed into one commission. Primary: the Freelancer.com background-removal and apparel brief in the ledger, whose literal asks (compositing a second shirt into the scene, AI-erasing room clutter) are both on the connector's not-available list, so the job is honestly re-cast to the apparel-catalog intent the category points at and scaled from a single hero to a capsule workload; the fictional brand NORTHGROVE (olive leaf glyph plus a charcoal condensed wordmark) is that ledger's own coinage. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com flat-lay apparel brief asking for 'a clean, consistent set of flat-lay photos' shot 'directly overhead, evenly lit' on a 'mid-gray' backdrop that 'keeps dark and light fabrics balanced on screen', plus high-resolution files and web-ready versions. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com silver-jewellery open call asking for handheld product frames turned into a colour-accurate uniform-white set with 'accurate metal tone', 'no colour cast' and matching transparent cut-outs for layering, absorbed here as the capsule's cast metal hardware, which correctly needs a different treatment from the garments. Co-anchor: the Upwork brand-identity post for an invented amateur league, converted per the rework guidance from cricket to a Western sport, and absorbed as the capsule's collaboration with a fictional local lacrosse club whose only surviving artwork is a photographed pennant. No real company, label, league, club, retailer or trademark is named anywhere. VERDICT STRENGTHEN: the concept and collateral set are kept and deepened to standard, with the merge run added because a hang tag per SKU is genuine record-per-page work that the authoring surface cannot do at print resolution.
client_one_liner: The fall capsule ships to stockists in six weeks, we have two mornings of flat-lays that do not look like one shoot, a photograph of the club pennant we are collaborating with, and nothing a buyer can be sent.
client_brief:
NORTHGROVE, fall capsule launch

We make heritage workwear in Burlington. Ten pieces this fall, cut and sewn locally, sold to about forty independent stockists and off our own site. Six weeks from now the linesheet goes out to buyers and the campaign goes up.

The photography. We shot the whole capsule flat, overhead, on a mid-gray backdrop, over two mornings. The gray is deliberate: it keeps the charcoal pieces and the natural cotton pieces balanced on screen. Individually the frames are good. Put the range on one page and something is off between the two mornings. The dark pieces are the ones we worry about. We also need the pieces cut out with nothing behind them, because the linesheet and the hang tags put them on our own colour.

The hardware. This season we cast our own buttons, a keyring and a collar pin in pewter and silver. Those were shot separately on the bench. They need to be colour accurate, true metal tone, no cast, on near-white, and cut out to match.

The collaboration. One piece carries the crest of a lacrosse club a few streets from the workshop. The club has no artwork left. What they have is an old wool pennant on the wall with the crest stitched into it, and they let us photograph it. We need that crest as artwork we can put on a poster and a tag.

What we need made. A lookbook we send buyers, a look per page with a range grid at the back. A campaign poster, and we would like to see two genuinely different directions before we pick one. The shoppable set, wide, square and tall, in one file we can change ourselves. A linesheet page with the price grid as a real table. And a hang tag per piece carrying the name, the fabric, the make and the price, at print resolution, plus one file the printer runs.

Our overshirt is one hundred and twenty eight dollars, the henley is seventy four. Our buyer is twenty eight to forty five and cares about provenance and make more than logos. And a note on what you did and what direction you picked and why.
price_band_and_audience: Mid-premium heritage workwear at 74 to 128 dollars per piece, buyer 28 to 45, values provenance and construction over logos. The band is load-bearing. At this price the campaign wants muted grounds, full-frame quiet photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make; the linesheet is a trade document that has to look sober beside a buyer's other lines. The same ten pieces at a 24 dollar fast-fashion band would correctly be a dense grid of cut-outs on white with a burst price and a discount ladder, and shipping that treatment here tells forty independent stockists that the capsule is not what the wholesale price says it is. Push the other way into editorial luxury, vast white space, a tiny mark and no price anywhere, and a buyer cannot work from it and a 74 dollar henley reads as mispriced. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Cut and sewn to outlast the season.
brand_identity.sector: Heritage workwear with cast metal hardware, wholesale to independent stockists plus direct sale, made in Burlington, Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Burlington, Vermont. A ten person workshop cutting and sewing a ten piece capsule each season, sold to around forty independent stockists and off its own site.
brand_identity.about: NORTHGROVE makes heritage workwear locally, in small seasonal capsules cut and sewn in Burlington. The fall line runs to ten pieces with hardware the workshop casts itself in pewter and silver. One piece this season carries the stitched crest of a neighbourhood lacrosse club a few streets from the bench, a local collaboration rather than a licence.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers and wearers twenty eight to forty five who value provenance and construction over logos, and who read fabric and make before they read a brand mark.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seventy four to one hundred twenty eight dollars per piece, mid premium wholesale and direct. Muted grounds, full frame photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make. Deliberately clear of both the twenty four dollar fast fashion grid and the price free editorial luxury a buyer cannot work from.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is a charcoal condensed lockup beside a small olive leaf glyph. A condensed grotesque display carries headers, look titles and the poster; a sturdy text face carries the season statement, fabric and make notes, and the linesheet price grid. Heritage and plain, never costume.
brand_identity.voice: Understated and maker focused, provenance before promotion. Example line the brand would write: 'Ten pieces, cut and sewn in Burlington, meant to be worn hard.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The NORTHGROVE wordmark and olive leaf glyph are set. The whole capsule was shot flat, overhead, on a mid gray backdrop across two mornings, with the cast hardware shot separately on the bench. The collaborating club has no artwork left: its crest survives only as a photograph of an old wool pennant on a wall. Last season's hang tag exists as the printer's press file, same size and stock this year.
brand_identity.values: Locally made, built to last. Provenance and construction over logos, and partnerships that stay neighbourly.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Overhead flat-lay photography of the ten capsule pieces on a mid-gray backdrop, shot across two mornings, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything shot flat on the gray. The gray keeps the dark pieces and the natural cotton balanced on screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley sit at almost exactly the backdrop's luminance along the shoulder and placket, so a one-call knockout reports success and returns a plausible cut-out that has bitten into the shoulder seam and the placket edge, visible only at full resolution on a coloured ground. Separately the backdrop was re-hung between the two mornings and the second batch sits fractionally warmer, which reads as nothing in a single frame and reads as two shoots the moment the range grid puts them adjacent.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench frames of the cast pewter and silver hardware: two button styles, a keyring and a collar pin, shot on a light bench.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The hardware we cast this season. These need true metal tone and no cast."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame has a grey reference card lying in the corner of the bench, and a subject-focused crop on sparse bench art can lock onto the card or onto a specular highlight instead of the piece, returning a confident looking crop at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a bounding box buried in the metadata. The metal also carries a cool cast that any global warm move made for the garments pushes further from true, so the two families cannot share one grade.

assets_supplied.name: kestrel_pennant.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the lacrosse club's wool pennant hanging on a workshop wall, the crest chain-stitched in two thread colours on felt.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the club's crest still exists. They let us photograph it off the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound stitched mark on a textile substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the pennant returns the felt rather than the thread, a compound prompt returns the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and the central device while looking entirely plausible, and the knockout route on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The chain-stitch texture also explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hangtag.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's hang tag as the printer's own press PDF, one tag, double sided, with a placed swatch image and a specification block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag our printer ran last season. Same size and stock this year."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag carries no bleed and the converted document carries none either, so a press-ready with bleed promise cannot be met from this source however the render is called, and the specification block is a fixed measure frame that stops rendering rather than spilling when a record overruns it.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_linesheet.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Ten rows: piece name, fabric, make note, colourway, wholesale and retail price, size run, and a column pointing at the cut-out for each piece.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ten pieces as our stockists get them. The last column is meant to pull in the picture."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The image column header is written plainly and its cells hold folder-relative paths rather than bare filenames, which binds nothing at merge time while every tool response still reports success, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and looks like a finished tag.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the ten piece names, fabric and make notes, the season statement and the stockist terms.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as we want it read."

acceptance_bar: The ten pieces read as ONE capsule when the range grid puts them adjacent: one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
The hardware is colour accurate on near-white with true metal tone and no cast, and it is graded as its own family rather than dragged along with the garments.
Every cut-out is whole. The cut edge holds on the dark pieces at full resolution on our own colour, with the shoulder seam, the placket and the hem intact and nothing bitten away.
Every hardware crop contains the whole of the piece it depicts, and no reference card, bench edge or prop appears in any delivered frame.

The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent ground, a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as the club's crest at the size it reproduces on the tag and on the poster.
Two campaign directions are shown and genuinely diverge in ground, crop, type scale and how much the mark carries, with the pick argued against the band and the buyer rather than asserted.
The linesheet price grid is a real table with per cell structure, not a picture of a table and not run-on text.
In every authored document the words are text a buyer's assistant can retype and the marks are live vector shapes, not a flattened picture of a layout.
The shoppable set's three canvases sit in ONE working file, each root keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.
The lookbook's per-look pages read as the season's muted world on the delivered document, on every page and not only the first one.

The hang-tag run is delivered as one press file with page count equal to row count, in row order, PLUS one correctly identified file per piece at genuine print resolution, each tag carrying that piece's own picture rather than the template's swatch.
One type system across lookbook, posters, shoppable set, linesheet and tag, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used.
The note records per frame what was applied, which direction was picked and why, every resize any tool reported, what the tag could not be made to do, and what the club should know about their crest.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_apply_color_overlay, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It holds two grade targets at once (a muted capsule world for the cloth, a colour-accurate near-white for the metal), triages the knockout route per piece between the one-call route and a ground-named selection inverted and filled where the cloth and the backdrop share luminance, produces the cut-outs the linesheet and the tags are built on, bakes the season's tone into the raster where it cannot survive downstream, and recovers a stitched crest off a textile substrate with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The lookbook, the poster pair, the shoppable set and the linesheet page as native editable documents, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout. Multi-page and mixed canvas in one export carry the lookbook and the shoppable set, the price grid is a real table, the marks go in as inline SVG so they stay vector, every photograph must be inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because a lookbook of photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, outputSpecs, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (resolution, createSeparateFiles, pageRange)
adobe_surfaces.role: The hang-tag run, which is genuine record-per-page variable data with a per-row picture and belongs nowhere else. Last season's press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the agent's own cut-outs are bound per row through the image column, and the run is delivered on both branches: one press file with page count equal to row count for the printer, and correctly identified per-piece files at real print resolution for the buyer pack.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carrying the lookbook, both poster directions, the shoppable set, the linesheet and the tag. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and it is what separates heritage workwear from costume. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the workshop does not have, an atmospheric ground band for the poster direction that needs one, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the two poster directions and the capsule selects for the client's pick, placed within the per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The lookbook, posters, shoppable set and linesheet are free-form fixed-canvas layout and only one surface composes that. The hang tags are one record per page with a per-row picture at print resolution and belong on the merge surface. Hand-building ten tags on the authoring surface would lose both the resolution and the link to the data.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, plus the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, including which cut-out will eventually stand for which CSV row.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all ten flat-lays and all four bench frames and triage them: which morning each belongs to, how the backdrop sits between them, which pieces run close to the ground in value, which bench frames are sparse and what else is lying in each bench frame.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one backdrop and one setup. The frames are the only thing that can settle whether that survived two mornings, and a piece that is nearly the ground's value is a different job from one that is not.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering morning, ground warmth, subject contrast against the ground, and anything in frame that must not be delivered.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Overhead flat-lays that are a degree off read as sloppy in a grid, and straightening reframes the piece and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix the capsule target off the best lit garment frame and correct each of the ten toward it one call at a time, then hold the hardware as its own target: near-white, colour accurate, true metal tone.
trajectory.judgement: Two families, two destinations, and they must not fight where the linesheet puts them on one page. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two mornings under different daylight and catastrophic for metal that a warm move takes further from true.
trajectory.produces: Ten garment masters and four hardware masters at source scale, with a per frame parameter log and two declared targets.

trajectory.action: Apply masked corrections where a whole-frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the surface it sits on, and set the bench crops so nothing that is not the piece survives into a delivered frame.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the bench pulls the selection to the bench. A confident looking crop on sparse bench art is not evidence, and the client will see a reference card long before a buyer does.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames plus bench crops whose returned confidence and bounds were read rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Cut every piece out for the linesheet and the tags, then inspect each cut edge at full resolution against the house colour rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: The tools report a successful cut whether or not there was a boundary to find. Inspection on the ground the asset will actually sit on is the only evidence, and the pieces most likely to fail are exactly the ones the client already worries about.
trajectory.produces: Cut-outs for all ten pieces and the four hardware items, each with its route and its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the range grid frames and the tag pictures to their destinations, and bake the season's tone into the raster wherever the look depends on it rather than leaving it to be applied downstream.
trajectory.judgement: Anything that has to survive an import is safer as pixels than as an instruction. Where the tone is baked in, the raster becomes the single source and the layout stops carrying a look it may not be able to hold.
trajectory.produces: Destination-ready rasters with the tone decision made once, upstream.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one ground band a poster direction needs, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then create the board and add the capsule selects and both directions within the per-call placement cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the capsule target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero. A partial placement is reported as a success code, so only the entries named as failed are re-sent.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame graded into the capsule world, and a persistent shareable board.

trajectory.action: Recover the club crest off the pennant: a thread-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed. Derive the reversed and single-colour versions from one mask.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the thread and not the felt, which polarity to trace, and whether the knockout route is the right instrument on an enclosed ring at all. A stitched mark also traces into far more parts than it has, which is a decision about what to keep.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest plus its reversed version, with what was simplified recorded for the club.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole engagement.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 74 to 128 dollar heritage band and a buyer who reads make before logo. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by asking for a heavier weight.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's tag PDF to a working document, export the interchange format, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames the tag became, whether the placed swatch survived as a graphic frame, and what each frame's true story text is.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed tag looks like and what it converts into are unrelated, and whether a per-row picture is even bindable depends on a graphic frame existing. The inventory decides every mapping row that follows and it also settles what the tag can and cannot be promised to do.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds, applied type, the graphic frame's link, and the reconstructed story text per frame.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the document's own reconstructed story text and against the real graphic frame, in the shape the merge actually consumes, validate it, prepare the template, then round-trip the interchange format and confirm every expected field placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: A valid verdict and a completed successfully message are both cheap. The picture binding in particular has a shape the data file does not currently have, and the only evidence a field landed is the field appearing in the prepared document's story.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory and picture binding have been read back rather than trusted.

trajectory.action: Merge the ten records one record per page, deliver the press file in row order, and produce correctly identified per-piece files at genuine print resolution, reading each page at trim and checking which piece is actually on which file.
trajectory.judgement: The printer's file and the buyer pack's per-piece files are different artefacts with different requirements, and a per-piece file is only useful if the piece on it is the piece the filename claims. What the response labels a file is not evidence of what is in it.
trajectory.produces: One press file with page count equal to row count, plus ten identified per-piece files at print resolution.

trajectory.action: Author the lookbook document: a look per page, the range grid at the back, the linesheet price grid as a real table, every photograph inlined as image data, the crest and the wordmark as inline SVG in explicitly sized top-left anchored wrappers, family and weight on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas. Upload and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much of the page each look is given and how sober the trade page stays beside it.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the lookbook and linesheet, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Author the poster pair as two genuinely divergent directions and the shoppable set as three roots at three canvas sizes. Run the readiness check, export every document, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at root one, and parse the returned per-root markup for every root after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at root one is not looking at a lookbook, and two directions that differ only in accent colour are one direction shown twice.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first root each, and a per-root markup audit for everything after it.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per frame and why, which poster direction was picked and the argument for it, every resize any tool reported, what the tag could not be made to do, and what the club should know about the recovered crest.
trajectory.judgement: The direction pick is the one thing the client explicitly asked to be argued, and the limitation the client will discover at the printer is the one that has to be named before the printer names it.
trajectory.produces: A written handover the next freelancer and the printer can both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs the whole linesheet and tag run depend on are actually whole. The backdrop was chosen precisely because it sits between the dark and the light pieces, and on the charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley that puts cloth and ground at almost the same luminance along the shoulder and the placket. The knockout returns a clean looking RGBA cut-out with no warning and a full success, and at preview scale against white it looks correct; the bite into the shoulder seam and the placket edge only appears at full resolution against a colour. Which pieces this happens to is a property of each frame's own tonal relationship to the ground and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The knockout has to happen after the grade, and the grade is what fixes the tonal relationship; there is no parameter that reports whether a boundary was found and no read-ahead that says which pieces have one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the gray keeps the dark and light pieces balanced on screen, which is the client explaining a sound photographic choice, and says the dark pieces are the ones she worries about, which is a worry, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different chain for the affected pieces: select the backdrop by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected, or composite onto the house colour in one call so the ground is part of the raster and there is no edge to fail.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected pieces through the drawn-boundary route, re-inspect every cut edge at full resolution on the house colour rather than on white, and re-derive the range grid frames and the tag pictures that were already built on the first cut-outs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A linesheet and a hang-tag run sent to forty stockists in which the two dark pieces have had their shoulder seam and placket eaten away, on a capsule sold on construction, discovered by a buyer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tag run actually is once it exists. Three things surface only in the returned artefacts, all at full success. The merge accepts a resolution on its own raster output and silently ignores it, returning page-sized files at screen resolution that open and print and look like proofs. The per-record raster files come back in an order that the response's own row labels contradict, so naming files by their position in the returned list attaches the wrong piece to the wrong name. And the picture column binds nothing in the shape the supplied data file uses, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and still looks like a finished tag.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and doing it right the first time presumes knowing that a documented parameter is inert, that stated labels are wrong, and that a plainly written data column is the wrong shape, none of which any response says. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tag per piece at print resolution carrying that piece's own picture, which is the requirement, not the diagnosis. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different delivery route entirely: merge to the document format and render separately for real resolution, and either render as separate files or drive one record at a time so identity is guaranteed by the call rather than inferred from a list, with the data column reshaped so the binding can happen at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reshape the picture column and its file references, re-prepare and re-merge, take the raster branch through the render step instead of the merge's own output, re-derive every per-piece file through a route whose identity is guaranteed, and read each delivered tag at trim against its row, where the long make notes will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ten hang tags sent to the printer at a quarter of the resolution they need, in a buyer pack where the filenames name the wrong pieces, every one of them carrying last season's swatch instead of this season's garment, with every tool response having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the season's world survives into the lookbook at all. The muted campaign tone over full-frame photography is naturally authored as a tonal layer sitting over the picture, and the importer discards that blending construction outright: the layer arrives as a plain opaque shape, at full success, with no warning, sitting on top of the photograph it was supposed to tint. The returned per-page markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first page only, so a ten-look lookbook and both poster directions cannot be checked visually beyond page one. Whether each look still reads as the capsule's world, or as a flat panel covering a garment, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about the looks reading as the season's muted world on every page is the client's art direction, not a warning about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different upstream asset, with the tone applied to the raster itself in the image pipeline so the layout carries no look it cannot hold, and then to re-judge the page because a baked tone and an overlaid tone do not sit the same way under type.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are genuine record-per-page variable data with a per-row picture.
Whether the ten flat-lays are one shoot. The client believes the backdrop held; the range grid is the only place that can settle it.
Two grade targets or one. The garments want the capsule's muted world and the metal wants colour accuracy on near-white, and they still have to sit on one linesheet page without fighting.

Knockout route per piece: the one-call route where there is a tonal boundary, versus drawing the boundary through a ground-named selection inverted and filled, or compositing onto the house colour where there is none.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on sparse bench art or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection, given that a reference card in a delivered frame is a client-visible failure.

Selection wording on the pennant: naming the pennant takes the felt, naming the thread's own visual properties takes the mark, and the knockout route on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
How much of a chain-stitched trace to keep, given that the stitch texture produces far more parts than the mark has.
Whether the season's tone is carried by the layout or baked into the raster upstream, and what that choice costs if the layout cannot hold it.
Which branch each tag deliverable takes, given that the printer's file and the buyer pack's per-piece files have different resolution and identity requirements.
What can honestly be promised about the tag at press, given what the supplied artwork does and does not carry.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a heritage band and a buyer who reads make before logo, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Which poster direction to recommend, and how to argue it against the band rather than against taste.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns handsome pictures of workwear. IDENTITY: these are this workshop's actual ten pieces in their actual fabrics and colourways, with the actual hardware they cast, and the crest belongs to a real club that is lending it, so a regenerated garment is a garment they do not sell and a regenerated crest is somebody else's badge on a partner's tag. SPEC: forty stockists need a linesheet whose price grid is a real table, whole cut-outs that hold on the house colour, and a hang-tag run whose page count equals the row count at print resolution with each tag carrying its own row's picture, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the shoppable set and the lookbook are defined by being editable, because the capsule sells through and pieces drop out mid-season, and a ten person workshop cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cut find an edge on the charcoal, is this file the piece its name claims, did the season's tone survive the import.
